subject: Computing home ranges for individual segments and combining them using pkde

messages.author: 97cf40dd257a9d12
messages.subject: Computing home ranges for individual segments and combining them using pkde
parts:
Hey Chris 

I wonder if you could shed some light on home range segmentation questions. 
I read lots of conversation on here and the linked papers but I still have some questions (that might also be interesting to other people). 

Summarising what I read, I understand that segmenting my tracks is a good idea if it contains range shifts. I used segclust2d for this and it works perfectly. However, given my dataset (many different species), it's very difficult for me to decide on a minimum segmentation length. Can I simply over-segment my tracks, select the best movement model for each segment and then combine the segment akdes using pkde()? This would have the additional benefit of being better to compute in parallel. However, I understand that this come at the cost of smaller effective sample sizes...

Do you have any thoughts on this? 
Many thanks!
Tom

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Computing home ranges for individual segments and combining them using pkde
parts:
Hi Tom,

If I was going to do something like that, I would probably try to code something adaptive, like halving the minimum segmentation length per individual until the total effective sample size of the segments stopped increasing.

Best,
Chris
